A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gradient GA and contain readable text, equations, tables and figures. All 18 pages of v1, including Appendices A–C, and all 22 pages of v2, including Appendices A–G, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original molecular optimization experiments, including benchmark comparisons, convergence curves, generated molecules and retraining and gradient-normalization analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds surrogate validation, parent-selection experiments, comparisons with additional genetic algorithms, runtime measurements and a multi-objective pilot.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the surrogate architecture, gradient calculation, DLP sampling, mutation and retraining procedures. Appendix G adds a limited adaptation that optimizes the product of mestranol similarity and amlodipine MPO as a combined objective.

E1.justification: ZINC 250K and the six existing GuacaMol objectives remain. Appendix G adds an executed joint mestranol-similarity/amlodipine-MPO optimization task, extending task requirements without introducing another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds Genetic GFN and MOL GA as evaluated comparators across all six objectives at 2,500 and 10,000 oracle calls. These stronger GA comparisons substantially expand the comparative evidence. Existing comparator sets remain, including REINVENT, which already appeared in v1 Appendix A.2.

E3.justification: The original 2,500- and 10,000-call settings, retraining variants and benchmark metrics remain. New protocols include two 10% validation sets for surrogate analysis and 1,000-call parent-selection and runtime comparisons. The main experiment's explicit early-stopping description is additional disclosure, not evidence that its protocol changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained retraining and gradient-normalization analyses, Appendix D adds surrogate training/validation-loss diagnostics, Appendix E tests best-parent versus averaged-parent guidance, and Section 5.2.4 adds a computational-cost comparison. These substantially broaden investigation of the method's components and costs. The molecule examples promoted to Section 5.2.3 already existed in v1 Appendix B.

E5.justification: V2 removes Table 2's explicit statement about five independent random seeds and reporting means and standard deviations, although five-run information remains elsewhere. New Table 16 follows the existing five-seed reporting practice, while Appendix G explicitly reports a single pilot run without uncertainty. No increased replication of retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: Tables 2–15 retain their numerical results apart from equivalent rounding. New comparisons and analyses substantially expand the findings: Table 17 reports 2,500-call mestranol Top-10 scores of 0.513 for Gradient GA, 0.668 for Genetic GFN and 0.687 for MOL GA, with Gradient GA having higher diversity. V2 also adds parent-selection, surrogate-error, runtime and multi-objective outcomes.

T1.justification: The oracle definition, Langevin/DLP equations, gradient derivation, sampling formulation and diversity definition retain their mathematical content. V2 adds empirical investigations but no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central gradient-guided GA contribution, novelty claim, faster-convergence claim and reported improvement of up to 25% over vanilla GA. Multi-objective optimization is added as preliminary future work rather than a redefinition of the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5.2.2 and Appendix F newly acknowledge that Genetic GFN and MOL GA achieve higher optimization scores and argue for Gradient GA's performance–diversity tradeoff. Appendices D and E add interpretations of surrogate accuracy and the parent-selection tradeoff, while Section 5.2.4 discusses computational overhead. These materially qualify and extend the account of the method's advantages.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly describes early stopping for the main evaluation and provides runtime estimates: approximately 1 minute for GA, 2–3 minutes for Gradient GA and 4–5 minutes for unnamed RL methods at 1,000 calls. Core architecture settings, optimizer, training epochs and code-access information remain unchanged; the runtime comparison lacks hardware details.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations and focused discussion of Genetic GFN (Kim et al., 2024) and MOL GA (Tripp and Hernández-Lobato, 2023). Section 2 also expands its contrast with MARS and DST, emphasizing their use of individual molecules. The broader literature survey and central novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language edits and paragraph rewrites, gives Appendix A subsections descriptive titles, moves part of the molecule-example discussion into the main text, and removes the Impact Statement. Experimental subsections and appendices are added, but the original section sequence and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout. Figures 3–6 are regrouped, heatmaps receive new palettes and label formatting, Figure 7 moves from Appendix B to the main text, and Table 1 is substantially shortened. V2 also adds Figure 12 and Tables 16–20.

improvement.justification: The stronger GA comparisons address an important omission in v1, while surrogate validation and parent-selection tests improve support for methodological choices. However, v2 retains broad superiority claims despite the higher comparator scores in Tables 17–18, weakens Table 2's statistical documentation, and provides limited runtime and single-run multi-objective evidence. The revision offers a useful but qualified net improvement.
